title: auth-api-401-429-debug-notes
body:
Context:
Quick personal scratchpad capturing debugging steps and breadcrumbs for recurring 401/429 errors users calling the hosted API. Seen over the last 48h for a handful of customers + internal QA. Trying to capture commands, error snippets, hypotheses, and next actions so we don't lose context during handoffs.

Symptoms observed:
- Intermittent 401 Unauthorized responses for otherwise valid API keys (most common during high error bursts).
- 429 Too Many Requests responses correlated with high request bursts from a single API key or route.
- For some customers, 401 appears only after a sequence of 429s (possible failover/rotating key behavior?).
- Internal metrics: spike in auth failures around 2026-02-27 04:20-04:40 UTC; region us-west-2 reporting higher rate.

Timeline (brief):
- 2026-02-26 23:10 UTC: customer A reports intermittent 401s.
- 2026-02-27 04:25 UTC: internal monitoring shows auth failure spike and corresponding 429 spike on /v1/generate endpoints.
- 2026-02-27 05:00 UTC: attempted repro using curl with same key -> sometimes 401, sometimes 429.
- 2026-02-28 11:30 UTC: rolled back a config change to the quota service (no obvious improvement).
- 2026-03-01 09:15 UTC: captured detailed logs below and started hypothesis checklist.

Commands tried (examples):
1) Basic curl (works sometimes -> 200, sometimes 401):
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}'

2) Repro script (bursting):
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abc123" -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":1}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done; wait

3) Intentionally malformed header (control test):
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abc123 " https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate   # trailing space -> returns 401 consistently

Observed raw error snippets (copied from gateway logs):
- 401 response body: {"error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"Invalid API key provided."}}
- 429 response body: {"error":{"type":"rate_limit_error","message":"Rate limit exceeded. Retry after 1s"}}
- Gateway logs: authz-check failed: token-expiry=false, key-active=true, scope-match=true, project-allow=false (note: project-allow toggles unexpectedly in some runs)
- Edge LB logs: 502 spike coincident with 429 burst (possible backend saturation)

What is reliably reproducible:
- If Authorization header has trailing whitespace or is missing, 401 reproducible.
- High burst scripts trigger 429 quickly for single-key tests (expected behavior if quota is low).
- Waiting ~60s after hitting 429 often allows requests to succeed again.

What is flaky / puzzling:
- 401s that occur when header format is correct and keys are known-valid.
- Some keys that should be on the higher quota plan get 429 like low-tier keys (possible bad mapping of key -> quota plan).
- 401s that follow 429s in the same client session. Hypothesis: quota service or auth service returning inconsistent state (e.g., temporary flagging of key).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Key provisioning / metadata propagation delay: recent key rotations or billing changes not propagated to all auth gateways -> intermittent 401.
2) Quota service bug: under high load the quota lookup/authorization path returns a temporary "deny" or throttles with wrong status code (should be 429 but sometimes 401).
3) Time skew / token TTL mismatch: if service clocks drift, we might incorrectly treat a key as expired (less likely; keys are static but internal caches might store expiry).
4) Header normalization/parsing bug in edge LB: trailing spaces or chunked encoding leads to header being parsed incorrectly -> 401.
5) Customer misconfiguration: client rotating keys or using a stale cached key without noticing (we've seen this but does not explain internal-only errors).
6) RBAC/project mapping issue: key belongs to project X but our route expects project-level allow list and mapping fails -> gateway reports auth error.

Quick checks to validate hypotheses (what I ran / to run):
- Check key metadata in Auth DB for affected keys (plan, active flag, last update). -> (TODO: run internal query authdb.getKey(sk-prod-abc123))
- Replay requests through local proxy that logs full headers to ensure no trailing whitespace or encoding issues.
- Check quota-service logs around spike times for cached-deny or cache-evictions.
- Verify time skew across auth nodes: ntp status on auth-gw-*.
- Cross-check billing/plan mapping table for keys that saw unexpected 429s.
- Inspect rollout history: any recent deploys to auth or quota services between 2026-02-26 and 2026-02-27? (Looking at git log: infra/auth-service PR #447 merged 2026-02-26 22:45 UTC)

Notes from quick log digs:
- Quota service instances show frequent cache-miss traffic at 04:20 UTC; miss -> sync to primary -> slight delay (tens to hundreds ms).
- There are a handful of 403/401s in auth-gateway logs preceded by quota-service errors (500) at the same timestamp. Suggests cascading failure: quota service error leads gateway to treat as auth failure.
- Auth DB shows last_modified for a subset of keys at 2026-02-26 22:40 UTC (aligns with a provisioning job run). Some keys show last_modified= "2026-02-26T22:40:10Z" while others older -> propagation incomplete.

Immediate mitigation ideas (safe, reversible):
- Increase quota-service cache TTL for reads to reduce lookup load during bursts (risk: stale data longer).
- Add more informative logging in gateway for "auth failure reason" to separate 401 vs 429 causation (already planned).
- Roll back the provisioning job if it correlates with when keys became inconsistent.
- Add soft-fail behavior: if quota service returns 5xx, gateway should return 429 (or 503) rather than 401 to avoid misleading clients.

Longer-term fixes / action items:
- Ensure key metadata propagation is strongly consistent or implement versioned metadata with deterministic fallback.
- Harden quota-service under load: autoscale, circuit-breakers, and graceful degradation path that does not flip auth decision.
- Add a synthetic test that replays a burst pattern and asserts no 401s for valid keys (CI job).
- Audit edge LB header parsing and canonicalization to prevent whitespace/trailing char issues.

Next steps (practical):
- [ ] Run authdb query for affected keys and paste results in JIRA ticket. (Assigned to Aisha)
- [ ] Reproduce with proxy that logs exact bytes (I will run this afternoon).
- [ ] Add canary code in gateway to classify failure cause and return 429/503 on quota-service errors. (Miguel to pick up)
- [ ] Schedule short postmortem if we confirm provisioning/job introduced instability.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Did the provisioning job run as part of scheduled backup or manual run? Who triggered it? (ask infra on-call)
- Are there customer-facing rate-limit headers ? X-RateLimit-Remaining / Retry-After presence/consistency? I saw Retry-After=1s in some 429 responses, but not consistently.
- Is there any relation to dedicated vs hosted customers? So far mostly hosted API tenants.

Pointers and links:
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/447
- Quota service dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/quotas
- Slack thread: #infra (02/27)

If/when we confirm root cause, I'll move this doc into shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/incidents/ and create a short postmortem. For now keeping it in my user scratchpad for easy iteration.

-- Jordan
